questions.prompt: Paetus gave me all the books which his father had left.
questions.answer: Paetus omnēs librōs quōs pater relīquisset mihi dōnāvit.

questions.prompt: They kept explaining to me the arguments which Socrates had set forth about the soul.
questions.answer: Dēmōnstrābant mihi argūmenta quae Sōcratēs dē animō disseruisset.

questions.prompt: He returned the sword which the king had given him.
questions.answer: Gladium reddidit quem rēx sibi dedisset.

questions.prompt: The farmer sold the lettuces which he had grown in his own garden.
questions.answer: Agricola lactūcās vēndidit quās in hortō suō aluisset.

questions.prompt: The woman blushed at the words which the young man had spoken.
questions.answer: Fēmina ērubuit ad verba quae iuvenis dīxisset.

questions.prompt: We admired the volumes which the poet had written in exile.
questions.answer: Volūmina mīrātī sumus quae poēta in exiliō scrīpsisset.

questions.prompt: He praised the wine which the guest had brought from Gaul.
questions.answer: Vīnum laudāvit quod hospes ex Galliā attulisset.

questions.prompt: The judge condemned the man who had betrayed the city.
questions.answer: Iūdex eum damnāvit quī urbem prōdidisset.

questions.prompt: She thanked the physician who had healed her sick son.
questions.answer: Medicō grātiās ēgit quī fīlium īnfirmum sānāvisset.

questions.prompt: He showed us the letter which his friend had sent from Rome.
questions.answer: Epistulam nōbīs ostendit quam amīcus Rōmā mīsisset.

questions.prompt: The boy hid the apples which he had stolen from the table.
questions.answer: Puer pōma cēlāvit quae dē mēnsā surripuisset.

questions.prompt: The mother wept for the children whom the war had carried off.
questions.answer: Māter līberōs flēvit quōs bellum abstulisset.

questions.prompt: The king rewarded the servant who had faithfully guarded the royal wealth.
questions.answer: Rēx servum remūnerātus est quī rēgiās opēs fidēliter custōdīvisset.

questions.prompt: We read the books which the old man had left to his heirs.
questions.answer: Librōs lēgimus quōs senex hērēdibus relīquisset.

questions.prompt: The maid brought in the food which the cook had prepared for the feast.
questions.answer: Ancilla cibum attulit quem coquus ad epulās parāvisset.

questions.prompt: He admired the fields which his ancestors had tilled with such great care.
questions.answer: Agrōs mīrātus est quōs maiōrēs tantā cūrā coluissent.

questions.prompt: The captive told of the dangers which he had endured in the mountains.
questions.answer: Captīvus perīcula nārrāvit quae in montibus tolerāvisset.

questions.prompt: They punished the boy who had disturbed the sleeping guests.
questions.answer: Puerum pūnīvērunt quī hospitēs dormientēs inquiētāvisset.

questions.prompt: The merchant praised the ship which had carried his goods safely across the sea.
questions.answer: Mercātor nāvem laudāvit quae mercēs suās tūtō trāns mare vēxisset.

questions.prompt: She kept the ring which her mother had given her before dying.
questions.answer: Ānulum servāvit quem māter sibi ante mortem dedisset.

questions.prompt: The senator recalled the promises which the consul had made to the people.
questions.answer: Senātor prōmissa commemorāvit quae cōnsul populō fēcisset.

questions.prompt: The teacher rebuked the pupils who had neglected their studies.
questions.answer: Magister discipulōs reprehendit quī studia neglēxissent.

questions.prompt: He said that thanks were owed to the enemy and to the war, because something was being done to free the state.
questions.answer: Hostibus bellōque grātiam habendam quod solitum quicquam līberāre cīvitātī fieret.

questions.prompt: An animal feels what it is that is fit.
questions.answer: Animal sentit quid sit quod deceat.

questions.prompt: He orders him to visit what states he can.
questions.answer: Huic imperat quās possit adeat cīvitātēs.

questions.prompt: He begs you to pluck from his heart this doubt that goads and stings him day and night.
questions.answer: Hunc sibi ex animō scrūpulum, quī sē diēs noctīsque stimulat ac pungit, ut ēvellātis postulat.

questions.prompt: If he wished to say anything about these matters, I gave him a chance.
questions.answer: Sī quid dē hīs rēbus dīcere vellet, fēcī potestātem.

questions.prompt: He passed a law concerning the murder which took place in the Appian Way.
questions.answer: Tulit dē caede quae in Appiā viā facta esset.

questions.prompt: He promised them his aid if they should be molested by the Suevi.
questions.answer: Iīs auxilium suum pollicitus sī ab Suēbīs premerentur.

questions.prompt: Themistocles used to walk the streets nights, ‘because he could not sleep,’.
questions.answer: noctū ambulābat in pūblicō Themistoclēs, quod somnum capere nōn posset.

questions.prompt: He waited at anchor till the rest of the vessels should gather there.
questions.answer: dum reliquae nāvēs eō convenīrent, in ancorīs expectāvit.

questions.prompt: Did anybody ever thank the gods ‘because he was a good man’?
questions.answer: numquis, quod bonus vir esset, grātiās dīs ēgit umquam?

questions.prompt: He vowed a temple to infernal Jove, ‘if he should rout the enemy on that day.’.
questions.answer: aedem Dīiovī vōvit, sī eō diē hostēs fūdisset.
